methodological_rigor.justification: The single-center retrospective cohort design is adequate for descriptive epidemiology and association testing, and the authors appropriately address immortal time bias with 3- and 6-month landmark analyses adjusting for age, PSA, tumor burden, and baseline SREs. Strengths include dual-radiologist adjudication of bone metastases and SREs with consensus arbitration, VIF assessment for multicollinearity, and a sensible univariate screening threshold (p<0.2). However, no a priori power calculation is reported, no multiplicity correction is applied across the many Cox models and subgroup tests, treatment comparisons are not supported by propensity-score methods despite clear indication bias, PSA is modelled only as a categorical variable (acknowledged by the authors), and the exposed subgroups in landmark analyses are small (e.g., n=12 for docetaxel at 3 months) which limits inference. Overall rigor is competent but with substantive gaps that the authors partially acknowledge.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual retrospective cohort study of 203 patients from one tertiary center, mapping to Oxford LoE 2b. The clinical question — characterization of SBM-HSPC prevalence and prognostic factors in a Chinese population — is relevant, and OS is a patient-centered endpoint. The main therapeutic finding (early NHA initiation associated with ~40–45% reduction in mortality) largely re-affirms class-level survival benefits already established in LATITUDE, TITAN, ENZAMET, and ARASENS, so translational impact is incremental rather than practice-changing. The epidemiologic finding of a lower contemporary SBM-HSPC incidence (6.09%) in a developed Chinese region has local policy relevance but is single-center.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is the applicable standard for this observational cohort. Many key items are addressed: setting and period, inclusion/exclusion criteria, variable definitions, outcome adjudication, handling of missing data (complete-case with <5% missingness), and a patient-flow description with Figure 1. Gaps include absence of a protocol registration, no explicit STROBE checklist reference, limited reporting of effect sizes with 95% CI for all comparisons (some χ² reported without CIs), and no sensitivity analyses beyond landmark timing. No data-availability or code-sharing statement is present in the manuscript text; while blinding may have removed journal-level statements, no repository, DOI, or shareable protocol is referenced.

novelty_literature.justification: Novelty is primarily empirical and population-based: a contemporary single-institution Chinese estimate of SBM-HSPC prevalence (6.09%) that contrasts a 2008 national figure, plus local characterization of prognostic factors. The core therapeutic signal — early NHA initiation associated with improved OS — reproduces established findings from LATITUDE, TITAN, ENZAMET, and ARASENS, and the identification of high-volume disease as a prognostic driver (CHAARTED criteria) is also well-known. There is no new mechanism, methodology, or first-in-class contribution; the work is incremental confirmation in an under-reported geographic cohort.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally readable with a logical IMRaD structure and a reasonably self-contained, quantitatively grounded abstract. The discussion is notably thoughtful about the paradoxical PSA finding and the limitations of single-center retrospective design. However, there are typographical and grammatical issues (e.g., 'statuse', 'l associated', inconsistent spacing before parentheses), the Results section repeats numeric content that duplicates Table 1, and some sentences on temporal incidence trends are speculative and overlong. Figure/table captions are brief but adequate; a few results statements (e.g., smoking HR = 1.48 in Discussion vs 1.52 in Results) show minor internal inconsistency that should be reconciled.

key_strengths: Landmark analyses at 3 and 6 months appropriately mitigate immortal time bias for treatment effect estimation
Rigorous outcome adjudication: dual-reviewer imaging and SRE validation with consensus arbitration
Transparent, thoughtful discussion of the counterintuitive high-PSA/better-survival association and its likely confounders
Contemporary single-institution incidence estimate (6.09%) for a developed Chinese region that contrasts older national figures
VIF reported to assess multicollinearity; prognostic covariates adjusted in multivariable Cox
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design with 203 patients and small exposed subgroups in landmark analyses (e.g., n=12 for docetaxel at 3 months) limit generalizability and power
Primary therapeutic finding (early NHA benefit) is confirmatory of LATITUDE/TITAN/ENZAMET/ARASENS rather than novel
No multiplicity correction despite many Cox models and subgroup comparisons; no propensity-score or IPTW analysis to address indication bias in observational treatment comparisons
PSA modelled only as categorical because of data capture, precluding spline/log-continuous analysis of the paradoxical association
No protocol registration, no data/code availability statement, and no STROBE checklist reference
Minor internal inconsistencies between Results and Discussion (e.g., smoking HR 1.52 vs 1.48) and typographical errors
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competently conducted but highly incremental single-center retrospective cohort that largely confirms established NHA benefit in mHSPC; appropriate for a tier-4 oncology journal after addressing minor reporting and consistency issues.
